intro: Your rule of 18 November (14-owner-calls.md call 13): nothing is withheld for missing a quality floor without your confirmation. These are the withholdings made before it, found in the app's code, settings-routes.json (a route whose condition reads "not offered" is hidden by SettingsRouteTable.offered), the stage notes and the DONE entries. Left out: your own calls in 14-owner-calls.md section 1, and anything dropped for money, licence, safety or memory. The session decisions in section 2 of that file were put to you for veto, not confirmed, so they are listed. Figures are from ArchiveProcessor/segbench-results/ unless another path is given; an interval is the paired 95% one. Routes that clearly lost to what shipped are grouped into one box per stage so they can be confirmed at once.

entries.feature: The "read poorly" flag for readers other than Apple Vision
entries.where: OCR/ReadQualityFlag.swift flags Vision readings only; the decision is in the body of 6f87dc24 (W46.post-read-quality-flag), which filed W46.post-read-flag-readers (open, behind W46.capture-warning and so behind nice-to-have).
entries.floor: At most 5% false alarms on good readings, a reading counted poor under 70 NES (post-read-flag.md).
entries.figure: Vision's own cut (0.9815) holds it: 10 of 21 poor readings caught with 3 of 75 false alarms on the 96, 179 of 231 with 7 of 249 on the capture ladder. For LightOnOCR, disagreement with Vision catches 8 of 11 poor readings on the 96 (73%, 43-90) with 4 of 85 false alarms; cross-validated 62% (56-68) with handwritten pages in and 82% (77-87) on typed pages only (post-read-flag.md). Qwen3.5 9B 33-36%. The same cut flags 21% of Gemini's good readings of damaged images.
entries.loses: No warning at all when LightOnOCR (the free handwriting default), Gemini, Qwen or any cloud route reads a page badly.
entries.ship: The disagreement flag on LightOnOCR, labelled "measured on plain photographs"; Gemini left out or shown with its 21% false-alarm figure. Unblocking W46.post-read-flag-readers from nice-to-have.
entries.why: LightOnOCR clears the false-alarm floor and catches most of its poor typed readings, and about three in five with handwriting in; it is the free handwriting default, where a silent poor reading costs the most. The label should say how much less it catches on handwriting.
entries.plain: A "read poorly" warning for readers other than Apple Vision
entries.what: The app can mark a page "read poorly" so that you know to check it. Today the warning exists only when Apple Vision did the reading. A page read by LightOnOCR (the free handwriting reader), Gemini or any other cloud reader gets no warning, however badly the reading went.
entries.tested: For LightOnOCR the warning compares its text with Apple Vision's and flags the pages where the two disagree. On your 96 pages it caught 8 of the 11 bad readings and gave 4 false alarms on 85 good ones, which is inside the limit of 1 false alarm in 20. In a wider check it caught about 8 in 10 bad readings on typed pages, and about 6 in 10 when handwritten pages were included. For Gemini the warning tested gave a false alarm on about 1 in 5 good readings of damaged pages, so it does not work there.
entries.released: LightOnOCR pages get the warning, with a note that it was tested on plain photographs and catches fewer bad readings on handwriting. Gemini stays without a warning. The work is already queued behind the nice-to-have list and would be moved up.
entries.plain_why: It meets the false-alarm limit for LightOnOCR. LightOnOCR is the free default for handwriting, where a bad reading that nobody notices costs the most.

entries.feature: Readers with no row on the reading chart: Apple's on-device model, the commercial services, and fifteen dominated routes
entries.where: settings-routes.json reading rule no-apple-fm; 04-reading.md section 3 (l.76) and section 4 (l.180-219).
entries.floor: Beating, or tying at lower cost, a route already on the chart.
entries.figure: macOS 27 on-device model 42.4 against Vision's 83.1 on the 96 (-40.7, -49.0 to -32.5), 33 of 96 pages looping (r1-foundation.md). Azure 89.6, Textract 86.6, Transkribus 82.5 against Mistral 4.1's 92.5 on 25 pages (Azure -2.9, -6.3 to -0.2). Fifteen hosted and cluster routes (qwen3-vl-8b, qwen3.5-122b-a10b, glm-ocr, lightonocr3-0.8b, ppocrv6-medium and others) each below a cheaper or faster route; paddleocr-vl1.5 superseded.
entries.loses: The choice of a weaker but familiar or already-paid-for reader.
entries.ship: A "show routes that lost" setting listing them with their figures.
entries.why: Each is beaten on the same pages by something the user can pick; showing them adds choices that only do worse.
entries.plain: Readers that scored below the ones already on offer
entries.what: The app lists a reader only if nothing cheaper or faster reads as well. Left off the list are Apple's new on-device AI model, three commercial services (Azure, Amazon Textract, Transkribus) and fifteen other open models.
entries.tested: Each was run on the same pages as the readers on offer and scored below one that costs the same or less. Apple's on-device model scored 42 against Apple Vision's 83 on your 96 pages, and got stuck repeating itself on a third of them. On 25 pages Azure scored 90, Textract 87 and Transkribus 83, against 92.5 for Mistral, which is on the list.
entries.released: A "show readers that lost" setting would list them with their scores. A user could then choose a service they know or already pay for, and would see that it reads worse.
entries.plain_why: Each one is beaten on the same pages by a reader the user can already pick.

entries.feature: A post-correction stage after reading
entries.where: settings-routes.json reading rule no-post-correction; 04-reading.md l.77-80.
entries.floor: A gain over re-reading with the same model.
entries.figure: The image-grounded corrector against re-reading with the 27B: -0.42 (-1.47 to +0.64) on the 96, but +1.47 (+0.55 to +2.63) on 120 public band readings; it worsens 4 of 57 and 10 of 120. Text-only correction gains 1.6 on the 96 and nothing on the public set, where it worsens 47 of 120 (ocr-postcorrect.md).
entries.loses: An image-grounded second pass that gains about 1.5 points on public material and ties on yours.
entries.ship: The image corrector as an optional stage, labelled with both figures.
entries.why: On your own material it ties; the public gain is real but small and costs a second 27B pass per band. Text-only correction stays out either way. A label would be a fair alternative if public-material users matter.
entries.plain: A second pass that corrects the text after reading
entries.what: After a page is read, a model could look at the image and the text together and fix mistakes. The app does not offer this step.
entries.tested: It was compared with reading the page a second time with the same large model. On your 96 pages it made no difference (a tie). On 120 public test pages it gained about 1.5 points out of 100 and made 10 of the 120 readings worse. A cheaper version that corrects from the text alone, without the image, made 47 of the 120 public readings worse.
entries.released: An optional step, labelled with both results. It adds a second pass by the large model on every page.
entries.plain_why: On your own material it changes nothing, and the gain on public material is small for an extra pass. Releasing it with a label is a fair choice if users with other kinds of material weigh more for you here.

entries.feature: Cascade triggers other than failure: log-probability and two-reader disagreement
entries.where: 04-reading.md l.79 and l.344; 10-kinds-and-routing.md l.50 (casc-disagree-0.5, "not built"). Owner call 5 made failure the only trigger and the Vision word-count trigger opt-in; these two were left out before that call by the session.
entries.floor: A consistent gain on unseen pages.
entries.figure: Log-probability shown only as a "check this reading" flag (ocr-logprob.md); disagreement and kind triggers "gain inconsistently on unseen pages"; the disagreement trigger "wants a larger test".
entries.loses: A second reading on pages the first reader probably got wrong but did not fail on.
entries.ship: A larger disagreement test, then an opt-in trigger beside the word-count one.
entries.why: Your call 5 already settles the cascade's design; these sit inside it and their figures do not argue for reopening it.
entries.plain: More reasons to send a page to a second reader
entries.what: The app can have a second reader re-read a page. On 6 November you decided this happens only when the first reader fails outright, with one opt-in extra for Apple Vision pages that come back with very few words. Two other triggers were left out by a session before that call: the first reader reporting low confidence, and two readers disagreeing with each other.
entries.tested: Neither was shown to help reliably. The disagreement trigger gained on some sets of pages and not on others, and the note says it needs a larger test. The confidence signal was only tested as a "check this page" mark, never as a trigger.
entries.released: A larger test of the disagreement trigger would come first, then an opt-in setting beside the existing one.
entries.plain_why: Your 6 November call already sets how re-reading works, and these results give no reason to reopen it.

entries.feature: A half-size retry when a cluster reader loops
entries.where: 04-reading.md section 3 l.91; section 2 Reading ("never a half-size retry on the cluster"); bench-corpus/loop-rerun-20261021.md.
entries.floor: Rescuing most looped pages.
entries.figure: Answered 351 of 1,573 looped pages on the cluster, 1,216 capped again, and the answers read at 4.2-11.0 NES pooled (bench-corpus/loop-rerun-20261021.md); on the Mac it led on three MLX loops (87.5), n 3.
entries.loses: An answer on a fifth of looped pages, almost all of it unreadable.
entries.ship: A retry step before the second-reader fallback, labelled with its answer rate and level.
entries.why: Its answers read at 4-11 NES, so it rescues almost nothing; the second VLM reader is the real fallback.
entries.plain: Retrying at half size when a reader gets stuck
entries.what: AI readers sometimes get stuck repeating the same words and never finish a page. One remedy is to shrink the image to half size and try again. On the cluster the app does not do this. It sends the stuck page to a second reader.
entries.tested: Of 1,573 stuck pages the half-size retry produced an answer on 351, about 1 in 5. Those answers scored 4 to 11 out of 100, so almost all were unreadable. On the Mac it did well on the three stuck pages tested, which is too few to rely on.
entries.released: A retry step before the second reader is tried. It adds time on every stuck page.
entries.plain_why: It rescues almost nothing. The second reader is what recovers these pages.

entries.feature: Cleaning the image before reading (shading, GCDRNet, SBB, DocRes, colour dropout, crop as OCR input)
entries.where: 02-ocr-input.md sections 2-3 (l.11-61), ocr-colour-dropout.md; 01-reading-copy.md l.20 (crop); section 2 OCR input. Owner call 6 covers only the reading copy.
entries.floor: The paired interval clearing 0 and a 0.49 NES gap (02-ocr-input.md l.25).
entries.figure: Five methods on 63 originals and the 96: none gained, several lost (Vision with SBB -6.4, -8.8 to -4.2; Gemini with shading -0.8, -1.6 to -0.2). Colour dropout on 40 pages: Vision +0.7 (-1.3 to +3.1), Gemini 3.7 -7.2 (-12.6 to -2.7); on the 16 pages with a real coloured mark Vision +3.4 (-0.1 to +8.4), but no cue picks those pages out. Crop on the originals -0.3 (-1.5 to +1.4). The Qwen3-VL 8B null is underpowered (about 5 NES).
entries.loses: An optional "clean before reading" setting; perhaps a small gain for Vision on stamped pages.
entries.ship: A per-route opt-in labelled with its measured change.
entries.why: No method gains on any reader measured, and the stamp lead cannot be aimed at the pages it helps.
entries.plain: Cleaning up the photograph before it is read
entries.what: Before a page is read, the image could be cleaned: evening out shadows, restoring faded text, removing coloured stamps, or cropping to the page. Five methods were tried and none is offered as a setting. (Your own earlier call covered only the copy you view, not the copy the reader sees.)
entries.tested: On your pages no method improved any reader, and several made reading worse. One cost Apple Vision 6 points out of 100, and shadow removal cost Gemini about 1. Removing colour may help Apple Vision on pages with a coloured stamp (about 3 points on 16 such pages, which could be chance), but it cost Gemini 7 points, and the app cannot tell which pages have such a stamp. For one small open reader the test was too small to rule out a modest effect.
entries.released: An optional "clean before reading" setting for each reader, labelled with its measured change. For most readers that change is a loss.
entries.plain_why: No method gained on any reader measured, and the possible gain on stamped pages cannot be aimed at the pages it would help.

entries.feature: DocRes cleaning on glare pages
entries.where: 02-ocr-input.md section 6 l.79, held as a lead inside the no-enhancement rule.
entries.floor: A result, not a lead: more than 6 pages, a significant pair.
entries.figure: On 6 glare pages, Vision with DocRes appearance +10.2 (+0.6 to +25.6), deshadow +9.2 (+0.2 to +24.8). The lead is Vision's only: on the same pages DocRes gives Gemini +0.5 (-0.5 to +1.9) and Qwen3-VL and GLM about 0 (enh-ocr-input.md); the 27B was not run.
entries.loses: A possible rescue of glare pages for Apple Vision readings.
entries.ship: The larger test, already filed inside W46.enh-small-reader-power (behind nice-to-have); then a glare-tag-triggered setting. DocRes needs a cluster GPU, so it would be a cluster setting.
entries.why: The largest gain in the OCR-input work, but for one reader on 6 pages; the filed test is the way to settle it.
entries.plain: Cleaning pages with glare before Apple Vision reads them
entries.what: A page photographed with glare (a bright reflection across the text) reads badly. One cleaning model, DocRes, is the exception to the item on cleaning photographs: it appeared to help Apple Vision on glare pages. It is held back as a lead that still needs a proper test.
entries.tested: On 6 glare pages Apple Vision's score rose by about 10 points out of 100. Six pages is very few, and the real gain could be anywhere from under 1 point to 25. It did not help Gemini or the two other readers tried.
entries.released: It would run only on pages marked as glare, and only for users with a cluster, because the cleaning model needs a powerful graphics card.
entries.wait: A larger test, already queued behind the nice-to-have list.
entries.plain_why: This is the largest gain in all the image-cleaning work, but it is for one reader on six pages. The queued test would settle it.

entries.feature: Rotation without Apple Vision: Tesseract, small local VLMs, PP-LCNet alone on right-to-left pages
entries.where: 01-reading-copy.md section 3 l.18 ("must not run").
entries.floor: Vision and the agreement rule (3 of 119 held-out pages wrong).
entries.figure: Tesseract OSD 62.7%, Qwen3-VL 8B 78.1% over all turns (rotation-routes.md); PP-LCNet alone flips 73 of 80 Hebrew turns.
entries.loses: A rotation route on a machine without Vision.
entries.ship: Rows labelled "below Vision".
entries.why: Every user of the app has Vision; these turn pages wrong a third of the time or more.
entries.plain: Turning pages upright without Apple Vision
entries.what: The app works out which way up each page is with Apple Vision, cross-checked by a second small model. Other ways of doing it were tested and are not offered.
entries.tested: Apple Vision with the cross-check got 3 of 119 test pages wrong. Of the alternatives, Tesseract got the turn right 63% of the time and a small open model 78%. The cross-check model used alone turned 73 of 80 Hebrew pages the wrong way.
entries.released: They would appear as choices marked "below Apple Vision". Every Mac that runs the app already has Apple Vision.
entries.plain_why: Every user has Apple Vision, and the alternatives turn a page wrong from about a fifth to over a third of the time.

entries.feature: Layout regions off newspapers: other kinds, handwriting, registers; Vision on regions; Apple's document request
entries.where: 03-layout.md section 2 l.15-18 and section 3 l.31 (calls 2-3, section 2 Layout); settings-routes.json layout-never-hands-registers; VisionOCRKit Prefs.swift figures() returns nil for Vision on regions off newspapers.
entries.floor: Beating the whole page.
entries.figure: On the 96, whole page 90.9 against heron 87.1 (-3.9, -7.7 to -0.3); tables with PP -9.1 (-18.3 to -2.3). On 16 hand pages 70.5 against 85.8 (-15.3, -28.2 to -4.4); on L4's 80 registers -10.8 (-14.8 to -6.8) (layout-photo-tables.md). Vision on regions off newspapers: 1.20% to 1.09% wrong at twice the time, no interval. Apple's document request 16.8 NES on L9.
entries.loses: A region pass that, where measured, loses text, apart from Vision's 0.1-point gain at twice the time.
entries.ship: A "read by regions" setting per kind, labelled with these losses.
entries.why: The losses are measured and large on handwriting and registers; Vision's one gain is a tenth of a point for double the time.
entries.plain: Reading a page region by region, for anything other than newspapers
entries.what: For newspapers the app first finds the columns and articles and then reads each region separately. Every other kind of page (letters, handwriting, tables, registers) is read whole. Reading those by region is not offered.
entries.tested: Reading by region scored lower wherever it was tested: about 4 points out of 100 lower on your 96 pages, 9 lower on tables, 15 lower on 16 handwritten pages and 11 lower on 80 register pages. There is one exception. Apple Vision on regions made slightly fewer errors (1.1% against 1.2%) and took twice as long.
entries.released: A "read by regions" setting for each kind of page, labelled with these losses.
entries.plain_why: The losses are measured, and they are large on handwriting and registers. Apple Vision's one gain is a tenth of a point for double the time.

entries.feature: DocLayout-YOLO as the detector for scanned newspapers
entries.where: 03-layout.md l.25, l.101 and call 1 (section 2 Layout picked PP-DocLayoutV3 for every newspaper).
entries.floor: Working on photographed newspapers.
entries.figure: On the 15 L9 scans (14 from one collection, mss34132) DocLayout-YOLO as the newspaper-ocr route leads PP-DocLayoutV3 by 4.6 (1.1 to 8.0), descriptive (layout-pair-newspapers.md). The photograph losses (40.1 on Skew, no region kept on 58 of 155 pages) are a different arm, YOLO with the app's region sort; the newspaper-ocr route was not run on photographs.
entries.loses: About 5 points on flatbed-scanned newspapers.
entries.ship: The newspaper-ocr processing route (not the app's YOLO arm) as a "scanned newspapers" detector setting, labelled measured on 15 scans from one collection and unmeasured on photographs.
entries.why: A measured gain for users with flatbed scans, common outside your corpus, on a small one-collection set; a label says how thin it is.
entries.plain: A different layout detector for flatbed-scanned newspapers
entries.what: To read a newspaper the app first runs a detector that finds the columns and articles. It uses the same detector for every newspaper. A second detector, DocLayout-YOLO, was passed over because one way of using it did badly on photographed newspapers.
entries.tested: On 15 flatbed-scanned newspaper pages the second detector led to text about 5 points out of 100 better (the real gain is somewhere between 1 and 8). Fourteen of the 15 pages are from one collection. In this form it has not been tested on photographed newspapers. The bad results on photographs came from a different way of using it.
entries.released: A "scanned newspapers" choice of detector, labelled as measured on 15 scans from one collection and not measured on photographs. Your own material is photographs, so this is mainly for other users.
entries.plain_why: It is a measured gain for users with flatbed scans, which are common outside your collection. The evidence is thin, and the label would say so.

entries.feature: Whole-page reading of newspapers for large readers (the detector is always run)
entries.where: 03-layout.md call 5 (l.105, l.124); section 2 Layout ("the gain is nil, not negative").
entries.floor: The reverse case: the detector is kept although it does not help.
entries.figure: 27B whole page 0.967 against raw regions 0.965 on 15 pages, no interval, an inference (03-layout.md l.124); the app ships the partition, on which the 27B was not measured.
entries.loses: The time of a detector pass that adds nothing for large readers.
entries.ship: A "read whole" choice for large readers on newspapers, or letting the solver's "faster wins on a tie" rule pick it.
entries.why: A tie on 15 pages; the session's tie rule in section 2 ("faster wins among equal cost", itself open to your veto) points to the whole page.
entries.plain: Letting large readers skip the layout step on newspapers
entries.what: This is the reverse case: a step that is kept although it does not help. On newspapers the app always runs the layout detector first, including for the large readers, which read a whole newspaper page as well without it.
entries.tested: On 15 pages the large open model scored 96.7 reading the page whole and 96.5 reading it by regions, which is a tie. This was measured with a slightly older way of cutting the regions than the one the app now uses.
entries.released: Large readers would read newspaper pages whole and save the time of the detector step, either as a choice or automatically under the rule that the faster route wins a tie.
entries.plain_why: The two are tied on 15 pages, and the tie rule the settings already use picks the faster one. That tie rule was itself a session decision that you can veto.

entries.feature: Other line layers: Orli base lines, Vision's document-request lines, block-emitting readers
entries.where: settings-routes.json placement hand-orli-ctc ("not offered; kept as a measured alternative"); 05-placement.md l.90, l.110-125.
entries.floor: Beating the shipped placer.
entries.figure: Orli lines 38.3% line pass (182 of 475), -4.6 (-14.9 to +4.2), a tie (place-hands-lines.md). Vision document-request lines -10.8 (-15.3 to -6.5) (place-print.md). Unlimited-OCR and Nemotron-Parse 2.0 keep 9.4-13.5% of truth lines whole.
entries.loses: Little: alternatives to a placer that does as well or better.
entries.ship: An option in the cluster placement setting.
entries.why: A tie and two clear losses.
entries.plain: Other ways of placing the text over the page image
entries.what: After reading, the app lines up each line of text with its place on the page image, so that text can be searched and selected on the page. Three other ways of finding the lines were tested and are not offered.
entries.tested: One tied with what the app uses. One was 11 points out of 100 worse. Two readers that produce their own text blocks kept only about 1 line in 10 intact.
entries.released: Extra choices in the cluster placement setting that do the same or worse.
entries.plain_why: One tie and two clear losses. Users lose very little by not having them.

entries.feature: A stamps and signatures layer
entries.where: 06-marks.md sections 2-3 ("not offered yet"); section 2 Marks. You put the two-pass route (W46.marks-detect-own) behind nice-to-have on 6 November; that the layer is not offered at all was the session's.
entries.floor: Detecting most marks.
entries.figure: Best detector YOLO11m: 8 of 45 marks at 0.25 (18%, 5-37%), 17 of 45 at 0.05 (38%, 21-60%), precision 42-53% (marks-detect.md). A whole page plus a YOLO box adds 0-3 marks per reader, p 0.5 or more.
entries.loses: A list of stamps and signatures on each page.
entries.ship: A layer labelled "finds about 1 mark in 5".
entries.why: At one mark in five with half its finds wrong, the layer would mislead more than help; your nice-to-have item is the route to a better detector.
entries.plain: A list of the stamps and signatures on each page
entries.what: The app could detect stamps and signatures and list them for each page. No such list is offered. On 6 November you put a better detection method on the nice-to-have list. Offering nothing in the meantime was a session's decision.
entries.tested: The best detector found 8 of 45 marks, about 1 in 5. Set to be more sensitive it found 17 of 45. At either setting about half of what it reported was not a mark.
entries.released: A stamps and signatures list labelled "finds about 1 mark in 5".
entries.plain_why: It would miss most marks, and half of what it listed would be wrong. The nice-to-have item is the way to a better detector.

entries.feature: The magazine kind "ranks nothing yet" for routes without the article rule
entries.where: 07-segmentation.md section 3 rule (a) l.67-78, call 5; settings-routes.json rule magazine-article-rule (5945c0b8).
entries.floor: A valid comparison: the students trained on the box and the older prompts lack the article rule.
entries.figure: Gemini 3.8 with g2 now ranks (93.8% of gaps against g1's 71.2%, seg-magazine-rule.md); g1, w1, c1 and the students still show figures without being picked.
entries.loses: A pick among the older prompts and the students on magazines.
entries.ship: No open item settles the rest: W46.seg-magazine-rule-redo and W46.seg-magazine-rule-app have shipped; c1 waits on W46.gateway-models-ok, and the students need a box they were not trained on (07-segmentation.md l.69-78).
entries.why: A validity gap rather than a missed level, already lifted for the Gemini route; the rest waits on the gateway and a fresh box, so ask again then.
entries.plain: Ranking the older methods of splitting magazines into articles
entries.what: Segmentation is the step that decides where one document ends and the next begins. In a magazine the unit is an article within an issue, and only the newest instruction, used with Gemini, tells the model so. For the older instructions and for the trained models the app shows their magazine results but does not rank them or pick among them.
entries.tested: With the new instruction Gemini places about 94% of boundaries correctly on magazines, against 71% with the old one. The others cannot be compared fairly yet. The older instructions lack the article rule, and the trained models were trained on the same box of magazines that is used for the test.
entries.released: The app would pick among the older methods on magazines from figures that are not a fair comparison.
entries.wait: One method waits for newer models to be enabled on the Stanford gateway. The trained models need a box of magazines they were not trained on.
entries.plain_why: No result fell short here. The comparison is not valid yet, and Gemini, the default, is already ranked.

entries.feature: Segmentation options that did not help: the document-split and feature models, few-shot examples, self-voting, a collection-facts block, letter cue c2, disagreement review on every route
entries.where: 07-segmentation.md section 2 l.15, l.87-88, l.275, SEG-4 l.290, call 3 option (b); section 2 Segmentation.
entries.floor: A measured gain over the shipped prompt.
entries.figure: Split and feature models 27.1% unchecked at 86.8 checks per 100 pages, against the 2B's 79.4% at 78.8 (seg-adapt-curve.md). Few-shot: no measurable gain at 1.43-2.01 times the input tokens (seg-adapt-fewshot.md). Self-voting and the facts block from seg-window-modality.md and seg-context.md, c2 no measured effect. Review on every route doubles the cost while the models err alike.
entries.loses: Settings that cost more and do not change the result.
entries.ship: Each as an opt-in labelled "no measured gain".
entries.why: None changes the result, and most add cost.
entries.plain: Extra options for finding document boundaries that did not help
entries.what: Seven additions to the step that finds where documents begin and end were tested and are not offered: two simpler kinds of model, giving the model worked examples, asking it several times and taking a vote, giving it facts about the collection, an extra cue for letters, and a review by a second model on every route.
entries.tested: None improved the result. The simpler models placed 27% of boundaries correctly without checking, against 79% for the app's small model. Worked examples gave no gain and used 1.4 to 2 times as much input. The second-model review doubled the cost, and the two models made the same mistakes.
entries.released: Opt-in settings labelled "no measured gain". Most of them cost more to run.
entries.plain_why: None changes the result, and most add cost.

entries.feature: The Mac Qwen3-VL 8B image pass on the no-key laptop dating route
entries.where: settings-routes.json dating qwen3-vl-8b-image-mac (a7068d5f, local baseline 57ddaeee); 08-dating.md call 7.5, "decided as recommended (section 2)", not one of your section-1 calls as pass 16 said.
entries.floor: "Once its quotes improve the year" over the text-only route.
entries.figure: On 55 documents with no year in their Vision text: strict reading gains 0 and loses 1; as a quote source gains 1 and loses 2 (sign test p 1.0); baseline 33 of 55 (60.0%), both 8B arms 32 of 55; false years on undated documents 20 to 21 of 90 (date-8b-local.md). On the traces it gains 0 (date-route-pipeline.md).
entries.loses: The only page-image dating a 16 GB Mac with no key could have.
entries.ship: An optional switch, off, labelled "no measured gain".
entries.why: No gain on either measure, and it costs a model download and its time.
entries.plain: Dating from the page image on a Mac with no cloud key
entries.what: When a document's text contains no year, a model can look at the page image for one, such as a stamp or a handwritten date. On a 16 GB Mac with no cloud key the only model that could do this is a small open one, which is a download. It is not offered, and the app dates from the text alone.
entries.tested: On 55 documents with no year in their text, the image pass got 32 right, against 33 without it. The number of undated documents given a wrong year was about the same either way (20 or 21 of 90).
entries.released: An optional switch, off by default, labelled "no measured gain". It needs a model download and adds time on each document.
entries.plain_why: It gained nothing on either test, and it costs a download and extra time.

entries.feature: Dating options below the baseline: trained 2B and 4B as defaults, typeface and paper dating, look-alike retrieval, an enclosure step, entity links
entries.where: 08-dating.md 7.4 (l.403-406), step 5 (l.81-83, DAT-4), step 3a (l.36-39, DAT-5), 09-entities.md l.367-369; section 2 Dating; settings-routes.json no-typeface-dating.
entries.floor: The shipped route's figure, or the simple baseline.
entries.figure: Trained 2B and 4B 38.9% (51 of 131) on years not in the text, against the shipped route's 47.3%; 0 of 50 owner-uncertain documents marked uncertain (date-model.md); the 2B stays as the chooser. Typeface ranges hold the year on 11 of 12 at a median width of 50 years (date-image-typeface.md). Retrieval 27 of 122 exact against 52 for the nearest dated document before (date-image.md). Enclosure: 0 of 3 owner enclosures found on every arm but the 27B (1 of 3) (date-enclosure.md). Entity links bracket 2 of 54 documents.
entries.loses: A coarse range for undated documents (typeface) and "Sent With" dating beyond the near-inert marker.
entries.ship: Each as a labelled option ("range, about 50 years"; "found 1 of 3").
entries.why: Each does worse than what ships or than the simple baseline; the trained models also cite no evidence, which your traceable rule needs.
entries.plain: Other ways of dating documents that scored below what the app does
entries.what: Five other dating methods were tested and are not offered: models trained on your tags used as the default, dating by typeface and paper, finding dated documents that look alike, dating an enclosure from its covering letter, and dating from the people named.
entries.tested: Trained models were right on 39% of documents whose year is not in the text, against 47% for the app's method, and marked none of 50 uncertain dates as uncertain. Typeface gives a range that holds the true year 11 times in 12, but the range is typically 50 years wide. Look-alikes got 27 of 122 right, against 52 for taking the year of the nearest dated document before it. The enclosure step found none of your 3 enclosures with most models and 1 of 3 with the best. People named narrowed the date on 2 of 54 documents.
entries.released: Each as a labelled option, such as "range, about 50 years" or "found 1 of 3". The main thing a user would gain is a rough range for undated documents.
entries.plain_why: Each does worse than the app's method or than a simple rule of thumb. The trained models also give no evidence for their date, which your rule on showing the evidence requires.

entries.feature: The 8,000-character Gemini entity prompt
entries.where: 09-entities.md l.133-149 and section 9 l.382-383; settings-routes.json gemini-entity8k.
entries.floor: A gain over the shipped call; withheld because its 3,000-character twin ties the shipped call, and it was never paired with the shipped call itself.
entries.figure: Sender 0.76 against 0.69, place 0.84 against 0.80. Paired: 8k against 3k +0.087 (+0.022 to +0.170) on sender, though on 88 of 138 documents the two are equal by construction (cached); 8k against the shipped tagging call +0.054 (-0.026 to +0.145), a tie. Rerun drift is +0.044 (0.000 to +0.115) on sender and -0.155 on place, which covers the place gap (ent-score-paid.md). Cost about $3.0 per 1,000 documents, an estimate.
entries.loses: Probably better senders and places on cloud routes.
entries.ship: A paired run against the shipped call on the cached owner truth, then the prompt as the default if it holds.
entries.why: Against the shipped call it ties, inside the rerun drift; a paired rerun would settle whether the sender lead is real.
entries.plain: A longer instruction for finding senders and places on cloud readers
entries.what: When a cloud model reads a letter it can also name the sender and the place. A longer and more detailed instruction for this was written and tested. It is held back because it was never run head to head against the instruction the app uses now.
entries.tested: It scored 0.76 against 0.69 on senders and 0.84 against 0.80 on places, where 1.0 is perfect. Set against the app's current instruction on the same documents, the lead is within chance, and repeating the same run moves the score by about as much as the lead. It costs about $3 per 1,000 documents, which is an estimate.
entries.released: It would become the default instruction on cloud routes and would probably give somewhat better senders and places.
entries.wait: One head-to-head run against the current instruction, on documents you have already checked.
entries.plain_why: Against what the app does now it is a tie so far. One paired run would show whether the lead on senders is real.

entries.feature: Names on Macs too small for the 8B (NLTagger, GLiNER2.5), and on pre-modern hands and early print
entries.where: settings-routes.json entities nltagger ("never offered… kept as the measured floor"), gliner2.5-base-spans-rule; 09-entities.md section 3 kind rule (e) l.42.
entries.floor: The 8B extractor's level; no floor is written for kind rule (e).
entries.figure: Sender F1 0.14 (NLTagger) and 0.24 (GLiNER) on 138 owner documents; even a perfect position rule reaches at most 35 and 60 of 138 named senders (ent-truth-owner.md, ent-score.md). Pre-modern Latin hands and early print 0.02-0.37 on L5 and L7 (ent-robust.md).
entries.loses: Any names on an 8 GB Mac with no key, and on medieval and early-modern material.
entries.ship: A row labelled "low confidence".
entries.why: At these levels most names written would be wrong. A cloud route covers the small-Mac case; no route, Gemini 3.8 included (0.12-0.37), covers pre-modern material.
entries.plain: Finding names on small Macs, and on medieval and early printed material
entries.what: Finding names (sender, recipient, place) needs a model too large for an 8 GB Mac. Two small tools that would fit were tested and are not offered, so a small Mac with no cloud key finds no names. Separately, no names are offered on medieval handwriting or early print.
entries.tested: On 138 of your documents the small tools scored 0.14 and 0.24 on senders, where 1.0 is perfect. Used ideally they could find at most 35 and 60 of the 138 senders. On medieval and early printed pages every method scored between 0.02 and 0.37, Gemini included.
entries.released: Names would appear on these Macs and materials marked "low confidence". Most of them would be wrong.
entries.plain_why: At these levels most names written would be wrong. A cloud route covers the small-Mac case, and no method yet works on pre-modern material.

entries.feature: Routing by kind on pages under the classifier's 0.8 confidence floor
entries.where: settings-routes.json kinds rule low-confidence-keeps-model; 10-kinds-and-routing.md section 3 l.38-43; section 2 Kinds. The 0.8 comes from K-kinds section 5 (W41.app-page-kind); no measurement behind it was found.
entries.floor: 0.8 on the top class.
entries.figure: 78 of 848 pages fall under it, 17 of them among the 29 pages whose hand differs from the rest of their document (kind-churn.md). Routing by true kind reads 97.26 against 96.47 for the best single reader on the 96 (kind-classifier.md section 4).
entries.loses: Kind routing on about one page in eleven, including most of the odd-hand pages it would help.
entries.ship: Route on the top class with an "unsure" mark, or the document prior (filed, not measured); a measurement of the cut itself.
entries.why: The floor itself is unmeasured; measure the document prior and the cut before choosing.
entries.plain: Choosing a reader by page kind when the app is unsure of the kind
entries.what: Before reading, the app decides what kind of page it has (typed, handwritten, newspaper and so on) and sends it to the reader that suits that kind. When it is less than 80% sure of the kind it does not do this, and the page goes to the general reader. No measurement behind the 80% line was found.
entries.tested: 78 of 848 pages, about 1 in 11, fall under the line. They include 17 of the 29 pages whose handwriting differs from the rest of their document, which are the pages this would help most. Overall, sending each page to the reader for its true kind is worth a little under 1 point out of 100 (97.3 against 96.5).
entries.released: Those pages would go to the reader for the app's best guess at their kind, with an "unsure" mark. How often that guess is wrong below the line has not been measured.
entries.wait: Two measurements: where the line should sit, and whether using the kind of the rest of the document works better.
entries.plain_why: The line itself was never measured. Measuring it comes before choosing.

entries.feature: A mixed-page pre-flag (ATRIUM or another), so the mixed switch acts only on flagged pages
entries.where: settings-routes.json kinds atrium-zero-shot ("not offered while the shipped classifier is kept"); 10-kinds-and-routing.md P4-1 l.86-88, l.61, section 6 l.113. Your call 3 set the switch off for its time cost; that is not this.
entries.floor: Beating the shipped classifier on kinds, and an established filter for mixed pages.
entries.figure: As a kind classifier ATRIUM is worse: 121 of 141 against 137 (p 0.000855), 638 of 895 against 723 (kind-atrium.md). On mixed pages its recall is 51-60% at 69.8% precision, covered-frame point estimates whose finite bounds run 18-95%, against the shipped classifier's 12-14% and Qwen3.6-27B's 23% at 99% precision. Qwen3.6-27B's pre-flag guessed the band on 7 of 14 pages (mixed-route-bands.md); the note says no mixed filter is established. Without a pre-flag the switch costs about 140 times Vision's time on every typed page (ocr-time-like-for-like.md, the like-for-like timing call 3 waited for).
entries.loses: A mixed switch cheap enough to turn on.
entries.ship: ATRIUM as an optional download used only as the mixed pre-flag, labelled with its recall, precision and wide bounds; then re-asking call 3 with the timing in hand.
entries.why: Its licence is no longer a bar since 17 November, and as a pre-flag its point recall is four times the shipped classifier's; the bounds are wide, so the label must carry them.
entries.plain: Spotting typed pages that also carry handwriting
entries.what: The app has a switch, "Read handwriting on typed pages (signatures, dates, notes in the margin)". You left it off because of its time cost. Without knowing which pages carry handwriting, it has to run the slow reader on every typed page, at about 140 times Apple Vision's time. A separate model, ATRIUM, could flag the pages that do carry handwriting, so the slow reader runs only on those. It is not offered, because as a general judge of page kinds it is worse than the app's own.
entries.tested: As a flagger of these pages it finds about half of them (51 to 60%), and about 7 in 10 of its flags are right. The app's own classifier finds about 1 in 8. The figures are uncertain: the real share found could be anywhere from 18% to 95%. A large open model was right on 99% of its flags but found only about 1 page in 4.
entries.released: ATRIUM as an optional download, used only to flag these pages, labelled with the figures and their uncertainty. You would then be asked again about the handwriting switch, with its timing now known. Its licence was the earlier obstacle and stopped being one with your 17 November call.
entries.plain_why: As a flagger it finds about four times as many of these pages as the app's own classifier, and it is what would make the handwriting switch cheap enough to turn on. The uncertainty is wide, so the label has to show it.

entries.feature: A sharpness or retake warning on the phone, and Gemini's quality score as a retake check
entries.where: settings-routes.json capture rule cap-guidance ("no tilt or compression warning"); 11-capture.md sections 3, 5, 7, 8 call 1; section 2 Capture. W46.capture-warning (a warning calibrated on real captures) is open behind nice-to-have.
entries.floor: A cut chosen on held-out real captures (11-capture.md section 7).
entries.figure: In-sample cuts catch 48-69% of losses with 17-34% false alarms on good pages; the Vision cut about 28% false alarms; Laplacian AUC 0.70-0.75 (capture-ladder.md). Gemini's score AUC 0.81-0.90 pooled, below a page-blind 0.83-0.91, and 0.50-0.80 within one defect, on 480 images of 48 pages.
entries.loses: A one-tap retake prompt on a blurred capture; the app shows static guidance.
entries.ship: A warning at the Vision cut labelled "in-sample, about 28% false alarms", or W46.capture-warning brought forward from nice-to-have.
entries.why: A warning at a 28% false-alarm rate would nag on good pages; the filed item calibrates on real captures. Bringing it forward from nice-to-have would also unblock the reader flag above.
entries.plain: A "retake this photo" warning on the phone
entries.what: When you photograph a page, the phone app could warn that the shot is blurred and offer a retake. Today it shows fixed guidance only. A warning set on real photographs is queued on the nice-to-have list.
entries.tested: The warning levels tried so far catch between a half and two thirds of bad shots, and also warn on roughly 1 good shot in 4. They were tuned on the same pages they were tested on, so real results would probably be worse. Using Gemini to score the photo did no better than a baseline that does not look at the page.
entries.released: A one-tap retake prompt that would also interrupt on about 1 good photo in 4.
entries.wait: The queued item, which sets the warning level on real photographs. Moving it up from nice-to-have would also unblock the "read poorly" warning for other readers, the first item on this sheet.
entries.plain_why: A warning that fires on 1 good page in 4 would nag. The queued item sets the level on real photographs.

entries.feature: Trained segmentation models for small materials (the kit gate's minimums)
entries.where: 12-training-kit.md section 3 l.49-62, calls 7.2 and 7.5; section 2 Kit.
entries.floor: Session-set: the paired interval's low end above -3 points, at least 267 known gaps and 10 held-out documents, two scored runs, a 3.2-point anchor margin.
entries.figure: The measured continuation's own next box, Lincoln box 2, holds 244 gaps and so fails the 267 minimum, though its errors fell from 17.2 to 4.9 per 100 gaps (-12.3, -18.8 to -7.4) (seg-kit-gate.md, seg-adapt-lora.md).
entries.loses: Any trained model for a material with under 267 known gaps or 10 documents: bound volumes and registers, which the note names.
entries.ship: Admit a model under the minimum with a "small held-out set" label and its interval shown.
entries.why: The one measured case would be refused despite a large, clear gain; a label tells the user how thin the check is.
entries.plain: Trained models for small collections
entries.what: The training kit trains a model on a user's own corrected material to find the document boundaries in that material. A trained model is used only if it passes a check, and the check needs a minimum amount of test material: at least 267 known boundaries and 10 documents set aside. A session set those minimums. Material below them, such as bound volumes and registers, gets no trained model.
entries.tested: The one real case measured would be refused. On a second box of Lincoln material the trained model cut errors from 17 to 5 in every 100 boundaries, a clear gain, but the box has 244 known boundaries, 23 short of the minimum.
entries.released: A model tested on less than the minimum could still be used, labelled "small test set" with its range of uncertainty shown.
entries.plain_why: The one measured case would be refused despite a large and clear gain. A label tells the user how thin the check was.

entries.feature: Item fields off the remote gateway, and three fields off their measured kinds
entries.where: ItemFieldPolicy.skipReason (Tagging/ItemFieldExtractor.swift:269-273): not run on a Local Agent plan or a local-model gateway. ItemFieldPolicy.withheld (l.250-265): byline and publication date only on published kinds, recipient place only on correspondence, "not measured on this kind". Title fills everywhere since your gate (6d1fb653).
entries.floor: The fill rule: Wilson lower bound 0.85 and point 0.90 on owner-checked pairs (FieldStatus.swift, item-fields-score.md).
entries.figure: On title, only the Gemini 3.7 image prompt fills (0.91, 0.86-0.94 stratified, of 147); GPT 5.6 Luna 0.82 (0.76-0.87), below the bar. The local Qwen 27B, 8B and 4B rows are "too close" or below the bar on the other fields and never fill title, but were scored on ABBYY text, which your 30 October rule bars, so no local route has a valid figure.
entries.loses: Every item field on the Mac and on a Local Agent plan, and three fields on kinds nobody measured.
entries.ship: Re-run a local model on Vision text or the page images and score it; then fill under a "lower confidence" status, which the Reader already shows for dates and containers.
entries.why: This is mostly a missing measurement rather than a miss; a local re-run is $0 but needs the heavy lock.
entries.plain: Title, byline and similar fields when working on the Mac only
entries.what: Item fields are the catalogue details of a document: title, byline, publication date, recipient's place. They are filled only when a cloud model does the work through the gateway. On a Mac-only set-up, or on the Local Agent route (a Claude or ChatGPT plan), they are not filled. Byline and publication date are also filled only on published material, and recipient's place only on correspondence, because those are the kinds they were measured on.
entries.tested: The bar for filling a field is about 90% right on pairs you checked. On title only Gemini clears it (91%), and GPT reached 82%. The Mac models fell short or were too close to call, but they were scored on the old ABBYY text, which you ruled out on 30 October. So no Mac route has a valid result.
entries.released: Fields would be filled on the Mac with no valid measurement of how often they are right.
entries.wait: A re-run of a Mac model on Apple Vision text or the page images. It costs nothing but needs the Mac's heavy-compute slot. If it comes close, the fields could be filled under the "lower confidence" mark the Reader already uses.
entries.plain_why: The Mac routes have no valid measurement yet. The re-run supplies one.

excluded: Your section-1 calls: dewarping and shading division not offered (call 6), the handwriting fine-tune dropped (call 7), hand pages flagged "needs a download or a key" (call 4), the mixed switch off (call 3), the hand layer only at 0.9 alignment and every hand page given a text page (call 12, which also covers why free-profile LightOnOCR hand text is not placed on the image), the failure-only cascade (call 5), the 4B entity extractor not offered and no sender from Vision text (call 11 and the 13 November walkthrough; section 2 repeats the 4B as vetoable, so the two sections disagree on whose it is), gemini-tagging-place (call 10), the rerun floor not deciding a pick (call 14).

A non-explicit date estimate that fails the evidence check is not shown (call 9) "until item 8.3 fixes the checker's false refusals". 8.3 (W46.date-evidence-check) shipped on 11 November, so the condition may now be met; worth a look, but it is your call, not this list's.
Dropped for money: the image pass only where the text gives no year, and no month or day image pass (about $0.51 per 1,000); the qwen3.5-27b reading rerun waits on the paid hold.
Dropped for memory: the Mac segmentation LoRA, the PP-OCRv6 hand detector on the Mac (32 GB).
Dropped for safety: crop and dewarp on the reading copy, under your no-removal rule.

Never measured, so withheld for want of a figure rather than a miss: direct-key rotation, the ChatGPT plan's OCR row, 27B readers on 32 and 64 GB Macs, Vision on non-Latin scripts, LightOnOCR off handwriting, names on non-correspondence and on a Local Agent plan, the 2B on 8 GB Macs, the right-to-left placement path, a handwritten-date reader.
No working signal, so nothing to ship: a glare warning (AUC 0.52-0.53 at best), a low-resolution flag, a trained reading-order model (Vision's order 0.972 ties the column sort's 0.971).
Lifted since: the text-only segmentation tier (your pick, 13 November); the title field (6d1fb653); the OpenRouter listing (W41.app-openrouter-unmeasured).
Routes hidden by provider terms (15-training-terms.md) are a privacy rule, not a quality floor.
plain_excluded: Not on this sheet: the decisions you made yourself, anything dropped for cost, memory, safety or licence, things that were never measured at all, and things that had no working version to offer.
also: One thing outside this sheet may be due. On 6 November you decided that an estimated date which fails the evidence check is not shown at all until the checker's false refusals are fixed. That fix shipped on 11 November, so the condition may now be met. It was your call, so it is not listed here. Say so in the last notes box if you want it looked at.
